pages.text: Creeeak! Downstairs, the oven door opened. It was the big fiery place where bread bakes. Mom peeped up the stairs. "Coco, I'm baking the first bread. Want to watch?" Coco burrowed back under the covers. "Yes... in a little while..."
Mom tugged gently at the covers. Coco shook their head and wouldn't move. "It's warmer in bed than by the oven!" Coco hugged the covers and slept on. Only the delicious smell drifted up.

Much later, Coco came down to the kitchen. The first bread had already been sold, and the shelf was empty. "I missed the first bread..." Under the empty shelf, Coco stamped one foot, then the other. Thump, thump.
Mom knelt on the kitchen floor, facing Coco. "That creak is morning calling. When you hear it, stretch your body long." Mom took Coco's front paws, and together they reached up high.

Two front paws—stretch! Two legs—stretch! Right to the tip of the tail! As Coco's heavy body stretched, it began to feel light. "Stretching chased the sleep away!" Mom smiled. "Oven door creaks—stretch, stretch!"

Jingle! Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, came in. "Coco missed the first bread? Ho ho! Tomorrow, Coco can watch first. I'll buy mine after that." Coco's mouth lifted into a smile.
At dawn the next day, the loft was still dim. Creeeak from downstairs! Coco sat straight up. Both front paws—stretch! Both legs—stretch! "Oven door creaks—stretch, stretch!" Coco called.
Coco came downstairs holding the headscarf. By the oven, Mom used her bread paddle to bring out the first bread. Steam rose. "The first bread! I saw it first!" Coco hopped and hopped.

The next day, and the day after, Coco jumped up at the creak. "One, creak means stretch! Two, take my scarf! Three, patter down the stairs!" Coco knew it by heart. Jingle! Grandpa arrived. "Coco's first today. Ho ho!"

Mom hugged Coco warmly from behind. "Up before the first bread!" At the creak, a long stretch helps the covers let Coco go. "Oven door creaks—stretch, stretch! Tomorrow I'll be first too!" Coco handed Grandpa the first bread.
